## 1–3. PMF, events, and the CDF

```{r}
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# c(): combines values into a vector, converting them to a common type when needed.
# sum(): adds vector entries; on logical values it counts TRUE entries.
# cumsum(): computes running totals in the current order.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# names(): reads or assigns names to vector elements or table columns.
# unname(): removes names or dimension names without changing the underlying values.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# abs(): returns absolute values; a small tolerance in an equality check permits floating-point rounding.
sales <- data.frame(x=0:5, count=c(54,117,72,42,12,3))
sales$p <- sales$count/sum(sales$count)
sales$F <- cumsum(sales$p)
kable(sales,digits=2)
ans <- c(Exactly_two=sum(sales$p[sales$x==2]),At_most_two=sum(sales$p[sales$x<=2]),
         At_least_two=sum(sales$p[sales$x>=2]),More_than_two=sum(sales$p[sales$x>2]),
         One_through_three=sum(sales$p[sales$x>=1 & sales$x<=3]))
kable(data.frame(Event=names(ans),Probability=unname(ans)),digits=2)
stopifnot(sum(sales$count)==300,abs(sum(sales$p)-1)<1e-12)
```

The probabilities are 0.24, 0.81, 0.43, 0.19, and 0.77, respectively. The first count reaching cumulative probability 0.50 is **1**, since $F(0)=0.18$ and $F(1)=0.57$. The supported values are integer counts 0–5; 1.5 is not a realization.

## 4. Moments and mode

```{r}
# sum(): adds vector entries; on logical values it counts TRUE entries.
# kable(): formats a data frame or matrix as a readable report table; digits sets displayed precision.
# data.frame(): builds a table whose named columns have compatible lengths.
# sqrt(): returns the nonnegative square root of a nonnegative number.
# which.max(): returns the position of the first maximum value.
# stopifnot(): stops execution if any supplied condition is FALSE; successful checks produce no output.
# abs(): returns absolute values; a small tolerance in an equality check permits floating-point rounding.
mu <- sum(sales$x*sales$p)
v <- sum((sales$x-mu)^2*sales$p)
kable(data.frame(Mean=mu,Variance=v,SD=sqrt(v),Mode=sales$x[which.max(sales$p)]),digits=6)
stopifnot(abs(mu-1.5)<1e-12,abs(v-1.25)<1e-12)
```

Mean 1.50 cars/day, variance 1.25 squared cars for the daily count, SD 1.118034 cars, mode 1 car. PMF and CDF values are unit-free. Computing summaries on `0:5` alone weights the possible values equally, and `var()` also applies a sample correction; neither uses the provided probability model.

## 5. Total sales and limitations

Expected sales over 30 operating days: 45 cars, assuming unchanged daily expectation. Linearity of expectation does not require independence. Variance 37.5 for the total would require zero pairwise covariances (independence is sufficient), an assumption not established by the summary. The six frequency cells are aggregate input, not the chronological raw daily records. Values above five are absent from the empirical summary; their absence does not establish impossibility for future days.
